Hi Alex,

Thanks for the onboarding call yesterday — Helix Health is excited to move forward. Before we lock the PO, legal/infosec have three asks we need confirmation on:

1) Region pinning: We need a firm statement on whether customer data can ever be processed outside the customer-selected region(s) (we will likely select APAC primary, EU for backups). Please be explicit about scenarios where transient processing could occur (e.g., analytics, backups, replications).

2) Temporary/ephemeral cross-region processing windows: Does Redwood perform short-lived cross-region processing for tasks like indexing, analytics, or cache warming? If yes, what are the maximum windows and how are they triggered/approved?

3) Subprocessors & evidence: We need a current roster of subprocessors that would see customer data, plus a timeline for when we can receive the SOC2 evidence and the transient-egress diagram referenced in the DPA appendix.

I've attached our requirements doc (helix_requirements_v1.pdf) with the specific compliance checklist. Contracts is copied because they will want the language in the DPA addendum to be explicit about any transient processing.

Can you confirm these points and, if possible, send the diagram and subprocessor roster within 48 hours? If any of this requires internal escalation, please advise the expected timeline.

Hi Marta — thanks for the clear checklist and for copying contracts. Short answers up front, then details and next steps below.

TL;DR:
- Region pinning: Customer data will be pinned to the regions you select for primary processing. Redwood will not perform persistent processing outside those regions for customer API inference requests.
- Transient processing: Short-lived cross-region processing can occur in limited, documented cases (analytics jobs, replication for short-term failover, or emergency ops). We will provide a transient-egress diagram (attached) and a short policy describing triggers and maximum windows.
- Subprocessors/evidence: Current roster + SOC2 evidence link below; full evidence pack available on request within 48–72 hours.

Details:
1) Region pinning and primary processing
We support region pinning by model endpoint. For Helix Health you can choose an APAC primary endpoint and an EU backup endpoint. All inference requests and KV cache storage are kept in the chosen primary region. Persistent storage (logs, audits) follows your selection and DPA settings.

2) Transient / ephemeral processing windows
Examples where transient cross-region work may occur:
- Analytics (batch telemetry processing) executed on a centralized analytics cluster for a bounded window (default max 6 hours unless otherwise agreed)
- Cache population or model warm-up to meet latency SLOs when traffic bursts trigger cross-region seeding (typically < 1 hour)
- Emergency failover where data is ingested into a geographically adjacent region to maintain availability (documented and time-limited).

All such activities are governed by our transient-egress policy:
- Triggered by scheduled analytics jobs, autoscaling events, or ops emergency
- Each window is logged with timestamp, affected customer(s), and data types involved
- Customers can opt-out of specific transient activities (e.g., analytics) via their DPA addendum
- We notify customers when an emergency failover occurs and provide post-event evidence

3) Subprocessors and evidence
Current subprocessor roster (brief): AWS (storage/compute), FastQueue Inc. (managed queue), TelemetryStack (analytics). A full roster and our SOC 2 report are accessible via the evidence portal. I'll ask Ops to prepare a packaged zip with the SOC2 redacted report, subprocessor ledger, and the transient-egress diagram.

Next steps / asks from our side:
- Marissa: can you open a HubSpot task (HLX-4721) to track the evidence delivery and DPA addendum? Link: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/HLX-4721
- Karthik/Laura: please confirm the list above and whether we can commit to the 48–72 hour evidence turnaround. If any legal nuance requires alternate language in the DPA, flag it.

I'll set a quick 30-minute call for Monday to walk through the diagram if that helps.
